activities.name: PR #437 — fix(deps): remediate CVE-2026-53550 in js-yaml
activities.summary: Raised the pnpm js-yaml override above the vulnerable <=4.1.1 range to js-yaml 4.3.0, closing Vanta/Linear POT-1660.
activities.description: Merged 2026-07-17 by Shambhavi Shinde on an agent-generated branch (cursor/pot-1660-vanta-vulnerability-fixes-3d9b) produced by the Cursor background agent, then reviewed by a human. Touches only package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml: the pnpm `overrides` entry for js-yaml is raised above the vulnerable `<=4.1.1` range so the lockfile resolves a single js-yaml 4.3.0, remediating CVE-2026-53550. Verified with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, `pnpm why js-yaml` (one resolved version) and `pnpm audit --json` showing no js-yaml finding. Part of the long-running Vanta vulnerability remediation stream tracked in Linear as POT-1660.

activities.name: PR #436 — fix: remediate websocket-driver critical vulnerability
activities.summary: Pinned transitive websocket-driver to patched 0.7.5 to remediate critical CVE-2026-54466 flagged by Vanta as POT-1966.
activities.description: Merged 2026-07-17, the first of two same-day websocket-driver fixes across the frontend surface (the VS Code extension got the sibling fix in potpie-vscode-extension#31). Written on a Cursor background-agent branch and shepherded by Shambhavi Shinde. The change pins the transitive dependency websocket-driver — pulled in through the socket.io/engine.io stack — from the vulnerable 0.7.4 to patched 0.7.5 via a pnpm override, then refreshes pnpm-lock.yaml so only one version resolves. Validated with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm why websocket-driver` and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level critical` returning no known vulnerabilities. Linear ticket POT-1966.

activities.name: PR #435 — fix: bump form-data, protobufjs, and dompurify to remediate Vanta CVEs
activities.summary: Three-package CVE sweep: form-data 4.0.5→4.0.6, protobufjs 7.5.8→7.6.4, dompurify 3.4.2→3.4.11.
activities.description: Merged 2026-07-07 by Shambhavi Shinde. The largest single Vanta sweep of the July cycle: form-data 4.0.5 → 4.0.6 (CVE-2026-12143), protobufjs 7.5.8 → 7.6.4 (CVE-2026-48712 and CVE-2026-54269), and dompurify 3.4.2 → 3.4.11 (CVE-2026-49458/49459/49978 plus GHSA-76mc-f452-cxcm, GHSA-cmwh-pvxp-8882, GHSA-gvmj-g25r-r7wr, GHSA-vxr8-fq34-vvx9, GHSA-x4vx-rjvf-j5p4). form-data and protobufjs are transitive — pulled in via axios and firebase — so both are held down with pnpm `overrides` rather than direct bumps. Only package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml change; there is no runtime code diff.

activities.name: PR #434 — Fix spec guardrail TypeScript build error
activities.summary: Added explicit GuardrailItem | null typing to spec guardrail normalization, fixing an implicit-any build break on the spec page.
activities.description: A ten-minute follow-up merged by Bharath Kumar K on 2026-07-03, hours after PR #433 landed. #433's guardrail normalization helper let TypeScript infer the mapped return type, which produced an implicit `any` and broke `pnpm build` under strict mode on app/(main)/task/[taskId]/spec/page.tsx. The fix annotates the normalizer as returning `GuardrailItem | null` explicitly. UI behaviour is unchanged; verification was `pnpm lint` plus `pnpm build`. A good example of a red-CI hotfix immediately trailing a feature merge in the spec surface.

activities.name: PR #433 — Align spec details view with enriched requirement metadata
activities.summary: Reworked the task spec detail page to render requirement priority, acceptance-criteria verification, file impact and structured guardrails.
activities.description: Opened 2026-06-26 and merged 2026-07-03 by Bharath Kumar K. The spec payload emitted by potpie-workflows had grown richer requirement metadata, and app/(main)/task/[taskId]/spec/page.tsx was still rendering the older flat shape. This PR surfaces requirement priority on the spec detail cards, adds a dedicated verification section for acceptance criteria, shows per-file impact (path, action, purpose), and preserves structured guardrail details including rationale and consequences. It also lightly normalizes malformed bolded subheading markers in streamed spec output so partial tokens do not render as literal asterisks. Search terms: spec guardrails UI, acceptance criteria panel, requirement priority badge.

activities.name: PR #432 — fix: restore mobile sidebar accessibility
activities.summary: Community PR rendering SidebarTrigger from app/(main)/layout.tsx behind md:hidden so mobile users can open the nav Sheet; still open.
activities.description: Opened 2026-06-25 by outside contributor LaibaFirdouse to fix issue #431 and still unmerged as of 2026-07-21 — the longest-open community frontend PR. Below 768px the sidebar renders as a Sheet controlled by `openMobile`, but the only SidebarTrigger lived inside AppSidebar, which is unmounted while the Sheet is closed, so navigation was unreachable on phones. The fix renders SidebarTrigger from the shared app/(main)/layout.tsx with a `md:hidden` class, leaving desktop behaviour untouched. Verified manually on New Chat, Chat, Integrations and Workflows. Keywords: mobile nav broken, hamburger missing, sidebar not openable on mobile.

activities.name: PR #430 — [Vanta] Fix Medium vulnerabilities in potpie-ui
activities.summary: Agent-authored PR resolving @opentelemetry/core to 2.8.0 for CVE-2026-54285 via a targeted pnpm override.
activities.description: Authored end-to-end by the Cursor GitHub App background agent — the PR author on GitHub is literally the `cursor` bot account, not a human — and merged 2026-06-17 after human review. This is one of three fully agent-driven Vanta remediations in June 2026 (#426 Low, #429 High, #430 Medium), each driven from a Linear ticket in the POT project; this one is POT-1642. It upgrades @opentelemetry/core to 2.8.0 for CVE-2026-54285 through a targeted pnpm override. The agent's own verification notes record that `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level moderate` still failed on unrelated pre-existing form-data, protobufjs and dompurify findings, which were later cleared by PR #435.

activities.name: PR #429 — [Vanta] Fix High vulnerabilities in potpie-ui
activities.summary: Agent-authored PR bumping @grpc/grpc-js 1.9.15 → 1.9.16 via pnpm override to clear two high-severity Dependabot findings.
activities.description: Opened 2026-06-12 and merged 2026-06-16, authored by the Cursor GitHub App bot rather than a human engineer — an agent-driven activity in the Vanta remediation stream, tracked as Linear POT-1579. It pins @grpc/grpc-js from 1.9.15 to 1.9.16 with a pnpm override to remediate Dependabot findings 151 and 152 (Vanta entity IDs 6a2b67d67e098647cecc6de7 and 6a2b67d67e098647cecc6ded). grpc-js reaches potpie-ui transitively through the Firebase SDK. The agent ran `pnpm audit --audit-level high`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build` before requesting review.

activities.name: PR #428 — fix: replace nested button elements with div in Sidebar
activities.summary: Community PR replacing invalid nested <button> markup in components/Layouts/Sidebar.tsx to stop React hydration warnings; still open.
activities.description: Opened 2026-06-11 by outside contributor LaibaFirdouse to fix issue #427, and still open as of 2026-07-21. Sidebar menu items rendered a button inside another button, which is invalid HTML: React logs `validateDOMNesting: <button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>` and emits hydration mismatch warnings on every dashboard load. The single-file change in components/Layouts/Sidebar.tsx swaps the inner element for a div with the appropriate role and handlers. Cosmetic in impact but noisy in the console; searchable as hydration warning, nested button, validateDOMNesting, sidebar menu.

activities.name: PR #426 — [Vanta] Fix Low vulnerabilities in potpie-ui
activities.summary: Agent-authored PR upgrading @ai-sdk/openai ^1.2.5 → ^3.0.69 to drop vulnerable transitive @ai-sdk/provider-utils@2.2.8.
activities.description: Opened and merged within twelve minutes on 2026-06-10, authored by the Cursor GitHub App bot — another fully agent-driven Vanta remediation, tracked as Linear POT-1535. Despite the 'Low' severity label it is the riskiest of the three June agent PRs because it moves @ai-sdk/openai across two major versions (^1.2.5 to ^3.0.69) to eliminate the vulnerable transitive @ai-sdk/provider-utils@2.2.8 (affected range <=3.0.97, Vanta entity 6a19d40dbc1dc504a44459a3). The agent gated the merge on `pnpm audit --audit-level low` reporting no known vulnerabilities plus a clean `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build`.

activities.name: PR #425 — feat: seed data (demo)
activities.summary: Revived the 88-commits-behind seed-data demo branch, retargeted it from main to staging, and resolved the workflow and spec-page conflicts.
activities.description: Merged 2026-06-10 by Deepesh Genani; supersedes the abandoned PR #386. The demo seed-data branch had fallen 88 commits behind main, so this PR merges origin/main in and retargets the whole thing at `staging`, which is what the staging deploy pipeline actually builds from. Two conflict classes were resolved deliberately: the four .github/workflows deploy YAMLs took main's security-hardened versions (pinned action SHAs plus Workload Identity Federation auth with key fallback) over the branch's floating action tags, and app/(main)/task/[taskId]/spec/page.tsx kept the branch's Generate-Plan handler with its explicit `regenerate` path through PlanService.regeneratePlan and stream-error fallback. The seed-data-specific work lives in commits 61ca996, 09c8b3c, 215dc3d and ac0a60f. This is the change that makes the scripted product demo reproducible for any account.

activities.name: PR #424 — fix(auth): close open redirect & token leak in sign-in redirect params
activities.summary: Genuine security fix: added lib/auth/safe-redirect.ts to stop an open redirect and a Firebase token exfiltration through attacker-controlled sign-in params.
activities.description: The most serious security defect fixed in potpie-ui to date, merged 2026-06-05 by Deepesh Genani, closing the vulnerability reported as potpie-ai/potpie#596. Two bugs: (1) open redirect — app/(auth)/layout.tsx called `router.push(decodeURIComponent(redirect))` on the raw `?redirect=` query value, so https://app.potpie.ai/sign-in?redirect=https://evil.com navigated an authenticated user to an arbitrary external site; (2) token exfiltration, the more severe issue — lib/auth/vscode-callback.ts used the untrusted `?redirect_uri=` value as the callback base and appended the user's Firebase token and customToken to it, so `?source=vscode&redirect_uri=https://evil.com` handed an attacker live auth credentials. The fix introduces a shared validator lib/auth/safe-redirect.ts exposing `getSafeInternalPath(raw, fallback)`, which accepts only same-origin relative paths and collapses absolute URLs, protocol-relative //host forms, backslash tricks, control characters and any non-`/` value to the fallback `/`, and `isLoopbackCallbackUrl(raw)`, which returns true only for http(s) loopback callbacks on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Landed with unit tests in safe-redirect.test.ts and vscode-callback.test.ts.

activities.name: PR #423 — fix(auth): open redirect & token leak (staging target, closed)
activities.summary: The staging-targeted twin of the open-redirect security fix, closed unmerged in favour of #424 against main.
activities.description: Opened at 10:56 and closed unmerged at 11:18 on 2026-06-05 by Deepesh Genani, twenty-two minutes before the identical fix landed as PR #424. The content is the same safe-redirect hardening for potpie-ai/potpie#596, but this copy targeted the `staging` branch. Because main and staging had materially diverged during the context-engine work, shipping the security fix into main first and letting it flow forward was judged safer than patching staging directly. Useful as a concrete example in the repo of the main-vs-staging branching confusion that also produced PRs #413/#414.

activities.name: PR #422 — Fixed low Vulnerablities (axios prototype pollution, ai-sdk provider-utils)
activities.summary: Upgraded axios 1.15.2 → 1.17.0 for CVE-2026-44489 and ai ^5 → ^6 to escape the vulnerable @ai-sdk/provider-utils 3.x range.
activities.description: Merged 2026-06-05 by Shambhavi Shinde. Two Vanta findings in one PR. CVE-2026-44489: axios 1.15.2 shipped an incomplete fix for prototype pollution in proxy configuration, so both the direct dependency and the pnpm override move to 1.17.0. CVE-2026-8769: the vulnerable @ai-sdk/provider-utils 3.0.20 arrived through ai@5, so the `ai` package is upgraded from ^5.0.107 to ^6.0.193 (resolving to 6.0.197), which pulls @ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.27 — outside the affected <=3.0.97 range. A major-version bump of the AI SDK done purely for CVE reasons, which makes it a useful precedent when weighing dependency risk against upgrade churn.

activities.name: PR #421 — Add frontend handoff for Potpie CLI browser login
activities.summary: Implemented the browser side of `potpie login`: cli_callback sign-in handoff, custom-token exchange, and a CLI success page.
activities.description: Opened 2026-05-29 and merged 2026-06-03 by Bharath Kumar K. This is the web half of the `potpie login` CLI flow: the sign-in page accepts a `cli_callback` parameter, the browser Firebase session is exchanged for a backend-minted custom token, and that token is POSTed back to the CLI's local callback listener before app/(auth)/cli-success/page.tsx confirms the handoff to the user. New modules are lib/auth/cli-callback.ts, lib/auth/cli-callback-url.ts and lib/auth/cli-success.ts with tests alongside. State and nonce binding on the callback (commit 02d90db) prevents a malicious page from completing someone else's login — invalid or missing CLI callback state must not complete login. Only useful together with the companion potpie PR that starts the local callback server and stores credentials; the two shipped as a pair.

activities.name: PR #420 — Med Vanta vulns fixed (uuid, protobufjs)
activities.summary: uuid ^9.0.1 → ^11.1.1 for CVE-2026-41907 with a broadened override, and protobufjs override 7.5.6 → 7.5.8 for CVE-2026-45740.
activities.description: Merged 2026-05-27 by Shambhavi Shinde. CVE-2026-41907 affects uuid < 11.1.1: the direct dependency moves from ^9.0.1 to ^11.1.1 and the pnpm override is broadened from `uuid@>=11.0.0 <11.1.1` to `uuid@<11.1.1` so any older transitive copy is also forced up. @types/uuid is deleted because uuid 11 ships its own types, and the only import site (v4 in the deprecated taskMock.ts) is unchanged. CVE-2026-45740 is handled by moving the protobufjs override from 7.5.6 to 7.5.8, the first patched 7.x release — later superseded by 7.6.4 in PR #435. Required a follow-up build fix (commit f072590) after the type-package removal.

activities.name: PR #419 — Removed linear env arg from code
activities.summary: Deleted the dead NEXT_PUBLIC Linear callback URI plumbing after the redirect moved to backend-managed, and tidied Sentry env wiring.
activities.description: Merged 2026-05-25 by Shambhavi Shinde. The Linear OAuth callback URI had already been removed from .env, but the frontend still passed the argument through app/(main)/integrations/linear/page.tsx and threaded the build-arg through Dockerfile, Dockerfile.Portable and all four deploy workflows (deploy-prod, deploy-staging, pr-cloud-run, upload-image). Leaving a required-but-missing NEXT_PUBLIC build arg in place meant staging images baked an empty value and the Linear connect button silently produced a broken redirect. The PR deletes the dead plumbing so the Linear integration relies purely on the backend-managed redirect, and cleans up Sentry env configuration across prod, staging and preview at the same time.

activities.name: PR #418 — Added debounced server-side GitHub repository search to Pot Sources
activities.summary: Replaced the click-to-Search repo picker in Pot Sources with debounced server-side search against /api/v1/github/user-repos; open against the events-revamp branch.
activities.description: Opened 2026-05-22 by Shambhavi Shinde and still open as of 2026-07-21 — it targets the long-lived feat/events-revamp integration branch rather than main, which is why it never merged on its own. The change reworks app/(main)/pots/components/PotSourcesPanel.tsx so the GitHub repository picker calls the backend `/api/v1/github/user-repos` search endpoint as the user types, debounced, instead of requiring a click on a Search button. It also adds compact search styling, a clear action, and centered loading and empty states with search-aware copy. Relevant to any question about slow or awkward repo selection when adding a source to a pot.

activities.name: Issue #431 — [Bug]: Mobile sidebar trigger is not rendered below 768px
activities.summary: On viewports under 768px there is no visible control to open the sidebar Sheet, so navigation is entirely inaccessible on mobile.
activities.description: Filed 2026-06-24 by community contributor LaibaFirdouse, severity Medium, reproduced on Chrome 149 / Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 22.18.0, pnpm 11.5.3 and Next.js 15.5.18 in local development mode. The mobile sidebar implementation already exists and uses a Sheet controlled by `openMobile` state, but the only toggle control is rendered inside AppSidebar — which is not mounted while the mobile sidebar is closed, producing a chicken-and-egg lockout. Net effect: on a phone, a signed-in user cannot reach New Chat, Integrations or Workflows at all. Fixed by the still-open PR #432, which hoists SidebarTrigger into app/(main)/layout.tsx behind md:hidden.

activities.name: Issue #427 — [Bug]: Sidebar menu renders nested button elements causing React hydration warnings
activities.summary: Sidebar menu items nest a <button> inside a <button>, producing validateDOMNesting errors and hydration mismatch warnings on the dashboard.
activities.description: Filed 2026-06-11 by community contributor LaibaFirdouse against the Dashboard/Home surface, severity Low (cosmetic), with three annotated console screenshots. components/Layouts/Sidebar.tsx renders an action button inside the menu-item button, which is invalid HTML; React responds with `validateDOMNesting(...): <button> cannot appear as a descendant of <button>` and a hydration mismatch warning on every load in both local and deployed environments. No user-visible breakage, but it pollutes the console badly enough to mask real errors during debugging. PR #428 proposes replacing the inner button with a div and remains open.

activities.name: Issue #355 — feat: up/down arrow key navigation for input history in chat
activities.summary: Feature request for shell-style ArrowUp/ArrowDown recall of previously sent messages in the chat composer.
activities.description: Filed 2026-02-25 by outside contributor Hari E and still open. Today, when no @-mention dropdown is showing, the arrow keys do nothing in the chat input. The request is terminal-like history: ArrowUp loads the previous sent message (saving the current draft on first press), ArrowDown walks forward and restores the saved draft past the last entry, typing exits history mode, and consecutive duplicate messages are not stored twice. The issue names the primary file to change as app/(main)/chat/[chatId]/components/MessageComposer.tsx. Frequently cited alongside issue #353 as the pair of chat-ergonomics asks from the community.

activities.name: Issue #353 — feat: export chat conversation as Markdown or PDF
activities.summary: Feature request for a Navbar export dropdown that downloads a conversation as .md or triggers browser print-to-PDF.
activities.description: Filed 2026-02-25 by outside contributor Hari E and still open. The chat Navbar currently offers only a Share button for email or public-link sharing; there is no way to take a conversation with you. The ask is an export dropdown next to Share with two options: Export as Markdown, downloading a cleanly formatted .md of all messages, and Export as PDF, which just triggers the browser's native print/save-as-PDF dialog against a readable print layout. Explicitly scoped as frontend-only with no backend changes, primary file app/(main)/chat/[chatId]/components/Navbar.tsx. Searchable as download chat, save conversation, export transcript.

activities.name: Issue #247 — Client-side sorting in AllChats instead of a sorted list from the backend
activities.summary: Community report that the AllChats page sorts backend conversation data in the browser rather than requesting an ordered list.
activities.description: Filed 2025-12-12 by outside contributor Aasheesh, with a screenshot of the offending sort call, and still open. app/(main)/all-chats/page.tsx pulls the conversation list and re-sorts it client-side, which is correct only while the whole list fits in one response — the ordering silently breaks the moment the endpoint is paginated, and it wastes work on every render. The underlying request is that the conversations API return a sorted list. Relevant background for any discussion of chat list ordering, pagination, or moving sort/filter concerns behind the API.

activities.name: Issue #246 — Dark mode: overlapping list rules in sidebar and unreadable black-on-dark-blue text
activities.summary: Dark-mode contrast and layout complaint: horizontal rules overlap list numbering, and black text on dark blue is effectively unreadable.
activities.description: Filed 2025-12-12 by outside contributor Aasheesh with full-window screenshots, and still open. Two distinct defects are bundled: in the sidebar and right-hand panels, horizontal rules collide with ordered-list numbering so the content reads as cluttered overlapping glyphs; and body text rendered near-black sits on dark blue panel backgrounds, failing contrast badly enough to be illegible. The reporter notes light mode improves contrast but the rule/numbering overlap persists there too, which points at prose/typography styles in app/globals.css rather than a theme token problem alone. Canonical reference for 'dark mode looks unpolished' feedback.

activities.name: Issue #213 — UI Component issue box greyed out
activities.summary: Fifth filing of the recurring inverted input-contrast bug: filled input text renders greyed out while disabled inputs render solid black.
activities.description: Filed by Nandan and still open — the fifth ticket in the greyed-out input cluster (#205, #207, #209, #211, #213), all carrying essentially the same one-line body: 'Input boxes used in the components have an issue where the text is greyed out when filled and when the input block is disabled it shows up as black.' The contrast semantics are inverted in components/ui/input.tsx: the enabled/filled state picks up a muted foreground token so typed text looks disabled, while the `disabled:` variant keeps full-strength foreground so unusable fields look active. The cluster is the canonical example in this repo of a low-severity UX bug that nobody owns, gets re-reported instead of deduplicated, and survives multiple design passes.

activities.name: Issue #211 — Component box is greyed out
activities.summary: Fourth duplicate report of inverted input contrast — filled text looks disabled, disabled text looks enabled.
activities.description: Filed by Nandan, still open, and opened within the same session as #213 — the two were filed roughly forty minutes apart, which is itself evidence that nobody was tracking the earlier reports. Same body as the rest of the cluster: input text greys out once filled, and disabled inputs render solid black. Practical impact is that reviewers cannot tell at a glance which fields on the pot setup and agent configuration forms are editable. Related duplicates were later filed as #305 and #344 in February 2026 and closed as such, but the root fix in components/ui/input.tsx never landed.

activities.name: Issue #209 — UI Component issue box greyed out
activities.summary: Third duplicate of the greyed-out input box report; text muted when filled, black when disabled.
activities.description: Filed by Nandan and still open, the third of five identical filings. The recurring symptom string to search for is 'input box greyed out' or 'text is greyed out when filled'. The affected surface is the shared shadcn-derived Input primitive in components/ui/input.tsx, which every form in the product consumes — new chat, pot creation, agent setup, source registration — so the visual defect is reported from whichever screen the reporter happened to be on. Because each report names a different screen, the tickets never got recognised as one bug.

activities.name: Issue #207 — UI component Input box greyed out
activities.summary: Second duplicate of the inverted input-contrast bug, filed forty minutes after #205.
activities.description: Filed by Nandan and still open. Identical body to #205, #209, #211 and #213: filled input text renders greyed out, and disabled input blocks render as solid black. Filed shortly after #205 in the same sitting, which is why the cluster reads as a burst rather than a slow trickle. Anyone triaging 'why does this form look disabled' or 'input text is grey' in potpie-ui should treat #205 as the primary and this as a duplicate. The fix is a token swap in the enabled and `disabled:` variants of components/ui/input.tsx plus a visual regression check.

activities.name: Issue #205 — Input box graying out issue
activities.summary: Primary report of the inverted input contrast bug in components/ui/input.tsx; four further duplicates followed.
activities.description: Filed by Nandan and still open — the earliest and canonical filing of the greyed-out input box cluster in potpie-ai/potpie-ui. Symptom: 'Input boxes used in the components have an issue where the text is greyed out when filled and when the input block is disabled it shows up as black.' The enabled and disabled foreground tokens on the shared Input primitive are effectively swapped, so filled fields read as inert and disabled fields read as editable. Four near-identical duplicates followed (#207, #209, #211, #213) plus two more in February 2026 (#305, #344, both closed as duplicates on 2026-02-23) — six re-reports and no fix, which makes this the best in-repo illustration of a bug pattern that recurs because it has no owner.

activities.name: Commit 182697d — fix(demo): make Start Implementation work for the demo recipe
activities.summary: Wired the Start Implementation action into the scripted demo recipe so the seeded flow completes end to end.
activities.description: Committed by Nandan on 2026-06-10 to feat/seed-data, immediately after PR #425 merged. Before this, the seeded demo would render the plan but the Start Implementation button dead-ended because the demo recipe had no handler bound for the implementation step, breaking the walkthrough at the most important moment. The fix threads the demo build flow through lib/mock/demoBuildFlow.ts so the button advances the scripted run. Together with e94854e this is the pair of commits that make the Potpie product demo reliably reproducible from a fresh account.

activities.name: Commit e94854e — feat(demo): enable redis DLQ demo flow for all accounts
activities.summary: Removed the account allowlist gating the Redis dead-letter-queue demo scenario so any signed-in account can run it.
activities.description: Committed by Nandan on 2026-06-10. The Redis DLQ scenario — the scripted 'messages piling up in the dead letter queue' investigation used in sales demos — had been gated behind a hardcoded allowlist of internal accounts, so anyone demoing from a fresh or customer account silently got the empty state instead. This commit removes the gate and enables the flow for all accounts. Search terms: demo not showing, redis DLQ scenario missing, seed data empty for new account.

activities.name: Commit 02d90db — State/nonce binding on CLI callback
activities.summary: Bound state and nonce to the CLI login callback so a forged or replayed callback cannot complete someone else's login.
activities.description: Committed 2026-05-29 on feat/cli-auth-integrations, part of PR #421. The first cut of the browser-to-CLI handoff accepted any local callback URL presented in the sign-in query string; this commit binds an unguessable state value plus a nonce generated at CLI-login start and validates both in lib/auth/cli-callback.ts before the custom token is posted back. Missing or mismatched state now aborts the handoff rather than completing login. Landed a week before PR #424 hardened the neighbouring redirect_uri handling, and the two together define the security posture of the potpie CLI browser-login path.

activities.name: Commit be3119f — feat(qa): multi-batch QnA flow and pipeline double-run race fix
activities.summary: Implemented multi-batch clarifying-question rounds on the task QnA screen and removed the race that ran the pipeline twice.
activities.description: Committed by Bharath Kumar K on 2026-05-13 (PR #402). The task QnA screen previously assumed a single batch of clarifying questions; workflows had started returning successive batches, so answering the first round dropped the rest. This change makes app/(main)/task/[taskId]/qna/page.tsx iterate batches and carry the run id forward. It also resolves a double-run race in which both the answer-submit handler and the stream-completion handler kicked the next pipeline stage, producing duplicate spec generations and confusing, interleaved streamed output. Search terms: duplicate spec run, pipeline ran twice, QnA questions disappeared after answering.

activities.name: Commit e72a73f — fix(ci): deploy staging from staging branch
activities.summary: Repointed the staging Cloud Run deploy workflow at the staging branch instead of main, so staging stopped shipping main's code.
activities.description: Committed by Yash Krishan on 2026-05-12 as PR #414, superseding the closed PR #413. .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yaml had been triggering on pushes to `main`, so the staging frontend was actually serving main while engineers believed they were testing the staging branch — a confusing failure mode during the context-engine work when main and staging had diverged by dozens of commits. Follows the earlier revert 8f1f4ad which had put the staging deploy back on us-central1/potpie-frontend. Anyone asking 'why is my staging change not showing up' in this window should read this commit first.

activities.name: Commit 40b8648 (vscode) — feat: websocket implementation
activities.summary: Completed the Socket.IO transport for the extension, replacing HTTP polling for streamed agent output.
activities.description: Committed by Nandan on 2026-02-22, finishing the work started in 1ba3326 four days earlier. Before this the extension polled the backend for agent progress, which made streamed responses arrive in visible chunks and left long-running agent runs looking stalled inside the editor. This commit lands src/SocketIOManager.ts as the real websocket transport so tokens and tool-call events push straight into the webview. It is the direct ancestor of both the memory leak fixed in 6852eb0 (undisposed socket subscriptions) and the websocket-driver CVE remediations in PRs #30 and #31 — the same dependency chain the transport introduced.

activities.name: PR #31 (vscode) — Fix CVE-2026-54490 in websocket-driver
activities.summary: Extension-side twin of potpie-ui#436: pinned websocket-driver to the patched release to clear critical CVE-2026-54490 (POT-1968).
activities.description: Merged 2026-07-17 by Shambhavi Shinde on a Cursor background-agent branch, minutes after the sibling fixes potpie-ui#436 and vscode#30 — one Vanta critical finding fanned out into three Linear tickets (POT-1966, POT-1967, POT-1968) and three near-simultaneous PRs across the TypeScript repos. websocket-driver reaches the extension through the Socket.IO client used by src/SocketIOManager.ts for streaming agent output, so a vulnerable version sits directly on the live agent transport. Only the manifest and lockfile change. Illustrates the fan-out pattern of Vanta remediation across potpie-ui and potpie-vscode-extension.

activities.name: PR #26 (vscode) — Remediate CVE-2026-44705 tmp vulnerability
activities.summary: Agent-authored (Cursor GitHub App) remediation of CVE-2026-44705 in the transitive tmp package; still unmerged.
activities.description: Opened 2026-05-27 by the Cursor GitHub App bot — a fully agent-driven activity with no human author on the PR — and still open as of 2026-07-21, making it the longest-stale Vanta item on the extension. It targets CVE-2026-44705 in the transitive `tmp` package, which arrives through the extension's bundling and tunnel tooling. It was opened seven minutes after Shambhavi Shinde's human-authored PR #25 covering the same high-severity batch, and the overlap is likely why it was never merged. A concrete case of agent and human remediation streams colliding on the same advisory.

activities.name: PR #19 (vscode) — Added UI screens for debug agent flow in extension
activities.summary: Webview screens for the in-editor debug agent flow, stacked on the feat/debug-tools-integration branch; still open.
activities.description: Opened 2026-05-14 by Shambhavi Shinde against feat/debug-tools-integration rather than main, which is why it has never merged. It adds the webview UI for the debug agent experience inside VS Code — the panels a developer sees when Potpie investigates a failing test or stack trace in the editor. Paired with PR #21 ('Unblocked real debug agent flow, deleted demo flow'), which attempted to swap the scripted demo path for the real agent and was closed. Together the two are the record of the debug-agent-in-editor effort that stalled in May 2026; relevant to any question about why the extension still ships a demo debug flow.

activities.name: PR #13 (vscode) — Add conversation restore and sidebar UI updates
activities.summary: Persisted and restored prior conversations in the extension sidebar so reloading the VS Code window no longer wipes chat history.
activities.description: Merged 2026-04-08 by Deepesh Genani. Until this landed, the extension held conversation state only in webview memory: reloading the window, switching workspaces, or letting the extension host restart discarded the chat entirely, which was the single most complained-about behaviour in early dogfooding. The PR persists conversations through src/ConversationStore.ts and restores them into the sidebar on activation, alongside a batch of sidebar UI updates that bring the panel closer to potpie-ui parity. Search terms: chat history lost on reload, conversation gone after restart, extension sidebar redesign.

activities.name: Commit 5f51559 (vscode) — feat: agent improvements
activities.summary: Latest commit on the extension's main branch: a batch of agent behaviour improvements to tool calling and streamed output.
activities.description: Committed by Nandan on 2026-03-10 and, as of 2026-07-21, still the HEAD of potpie-ai/potpie-vscode-extension main — the extension's feature work has been quiet since March 2026 while everything after it has been Vanta dependency remediation. The commit tightens agent behaviour across src/ChatViewProvider.ts and the streaming path: tool-call rendering, terminal command allowlisting via src/TerminalCommandAllowlist.ts, and how partial agent output is flushed to the webview. Useful anchor for 'when did the extension last get real feature work'.

activities.name: Commit 6852eb0 (vscode) — fix: memory leak
activities.summary: Fixed a memory leak in the extension host from undisposed listeners/sockets accumulating across chat sessions.
activities.description: Committed by Nandan on 2026-02-27 on feat/agent-chores (merged via PR #7). The extension host's memory grew steadily during long sessions because webview message listeners and Socket.IO subscriptions created per conversation were never disposed — each new chat added another live subscriber to the same stream, so output was also delivered multiple times in long-lived windows. The fix registers disposables properly around src/SocketIOManager.ts and the chat view lifecycle. Symptoms to search for: VS Code slows down after using Potpie, duplicated streamed messages, extension host high memory.

activities.name: Commit 8580630 (vscode) — fix: Improve tunnel stability and DNS error handling
activities.summary: Hardened the local tunnel used to expose the extension's local server to the backend, with explicit DNS failure handling.
activities.description: Committed by Yash Krishan on 2026-02-02, part of the local-tunnel work that lets the Potpie backend reach the developer's machine so agents can read the real working tree. The tunnel would fail opaquely when DNS resolution for the tunnel hostname failed or lagged behind tunnel creation, leaving the extension stuck at 'connecting' with no actionable error. This change adds retry and explicit DNS error surfacing in the tunnel manager, and pairs with d6c787b (verify named tunnel, fall back to quick tunnel) and 5976f6f (trust backend tunnel requests, dynamic port routing). Search terms: tunnel stuck connecting, ENOTFOUND trycloudflare, extension cannot reach backend.
